notes: §1985:XV.3.2.3 SR10 (as amended by X3.23a-1989): an identifier-1 whose entry has or is subordinate to an OCCURS clause 'must be specified without the subscripting normally required'. FinalizeDebug sends both the identifier-1 and ALL REFERENCES OF identifier-1 operands to ProcedureTableBuilder.AddDebugDataTarget, which refuses COBOL6334 any subscript part on the operand or on any of its qualifiers; NamesDataItem resolves the declaration without the 'shall be subscripted' screen, so the bare table element is accepted. Probed at 85 on an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table: F1, ALL REFERENCES OF F2 (two-level) and the group R unsubscripted are accepted and fire with DEBUG-SUB-1/2 naming the occurrence (+0003 +0002); F1 (1), F1 (IX), F2 (SUBV), ALL REFERENCES OF F2 (1 2), F1 OF R (1) and ALL F1 IN T (2) are each refused COBOL6334; at 2002 and 2023 the statement is COBOL0902. The witness refuses ELEM (1).

next.reason: X3.23a-1989 (its change for page XV-5, a typographical correction, errata C160) deleted 'or indexing'; the rule still restricts identifier-1 of a USE FOR DEBUGGING statement. §1985:XV.3.2.3 SR10: 'identifier-1 must be specified without the subscripting normally required'. The 2023 standard has no USE FOR DEBUGGING statement: §2023:14.9.49.2 gives the USE statement four formats, 'Format 1 (file-exception)', 'Format 2 (reporting)', 'Format 3 (exception-name)' and 'Format 4 (exception-object)', none for debugging, and the words FOR DEBUGGING and DEBUG-ITEM occur nowhere in specs/ISO_COBOL_2023.md. The feature is dropped and no 2023 rule states this requirement.
